protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; two severable RULE-GOVERNED recordings in D-038 / D-039 / D-040 / D-041 form
summary: All eight cited digests match live bytes, and the verdict-class axis the dispatch singles out is exactly right for my half: both my v2 reviews returned ACCEPT with 0 blockers and 0 advisories, and both entries recite ACCEPT 0/0. The pair is genuinely severable, each entry forecloses ACCEPT-as-owner-recording twice over, and the owner names are three-way consistent across file 08, the entries and the recorded dispositions. I chased two apparent form gaps against D-039 -- no 'not SATISFIED' beside HARD-BLOCKED, and no 'Mark SATISFIED' among the rejected alternatives -- and measurement dissolved both: across 38 adopted entries only one carries the SATISFIED alternative and only three say 'not SATISFIED' anywhere, so neither is a convention this pair departs from. Nothing else survives.
whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: bb119dce5d319140e3540cdb07196d96bc5950c93b1088f18e3cbb942a7e7a7c both times, matching the dispatch. No drift.

The attack 'verdict class misstated (must be ACCEPT, not ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES)' fails on my half, and I can state this from my own bytes rather than from the entry. My DR-002 v2 verdict is ACCEPT with blockers 0 and advisories 0; my DR-004 v2 verdict is the same. Both entries recite 'ACCEPT 0/0'. This is the inverse of the defect I raised as C2-D039-01, where an entry called an ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES an ACCEPT, and it does not recur in either direction.

The attack 'cited digests do not match live bytes' fails on all eight: DR-002 v2 301ea338…, DR-002 Claude 2 v2 4619a113…, DR-002 Codex v2 b3be13e2…, DR-004 v2 2866dd87…, DR-004 Claude 2 v2 a2ab3306…, DR-004 Codex v2 9813080054…, COORD d78fe15b…, file 08 6547e6ac…. Each measured by me against live bytes; the two Codex verdicts were hashed without being opened.

The attack 'treats ACCEPT as owner recording' fails, foreclosed twice in each entry's clause 1 -- 'This is not owner recording. An ACCEPT verdict is not owner recording.' -- and once more in each Alternatives list as 'Treat ACCEPT as owner recording. Rejected.' The header adds '**Does not** owner-record.'

The attack 'coordinator becomes recording authority' fails, and it matters most on D-049 because file 08 names the V1 coordinator a co-owner of DR-002, which makes the distance between drafting, reviewing and recording shortest on that row. The entry does not exploit it: 'Owner remains Evidence authority + V1 coordinator. This is not owner recording.' I raised the same structural risk on D-041's DR-003 row and it is handled the same way here.

The owner names are three-way consistent, which I checked at the bytes rather than assuming. File 08's owner cells read 'Evidence authority + V1 coordinator' for DR-002 and 'Evidence/retention authority' for DR-004; D-049 and D-050 state those exact strings; and the recorded dispositions' ownerWhoMustRecord fields state them again with the file-08 citation.

The attack 'silent SATISFIED or condition-1 discharge' fails. The header states '**Does not** mark SATISFIED', each clause 2 keeps its row HARD-BLOCKED -- which the register's vocabulary makes mutually exclusive with SATISFIED -- and each states 'Condition 1 does not discharge until those owners record' / 'until the owner records', followed by 'Conditions 2–5 remain. Condition 5 remains the only implementation authorization.' The rows' live standing confirms the claim: DR-002 and DR-004 are both HARD-BLOCKED in file 08 today.

D-049's acceptance-criteria statement is accurate against both the recorded disposition and the register: 'AC-1, AC-3, and AC-4 stay not discharged.' That matches the v2 disposition's acceptanceCriteriaStanding, which I verified criterion by criterion at the v1 and v2 reviews, and file 08's DR-002 cell, which records AC-2 satisfied with AC-1 not discharged and AC-3/AC-4 open.

The attack 'treats section31 v4 as the Phase-1A packet' fails twice in D-050: clause 2 states 'The eight-bullet Phase-1A packet stays owed. section31 v4 stays the binding instrument, not the packet', and the Alternatives reject 'Treat section31 v4 as the packet. Rejected: D-045 and the disposition both refuse that.' Both halves of that citation are true — D-045 records the instrument without promoting it, and the v2 disposition refuses promotion in three separate fields.

The attack 'unsverable bundle (D-025 defect)' fails at three levels. The header states 'Two severable entries' and 'Adopting or overturning one does not adopt or overturn the other.' Each entry carries its own Subject line naming one artifact 'only' and an explicit Severable line naming the other entry. Each has its own Decision, Alternatives, Readiness effect, Reversibility and overturn commit, C-D049 and C-D050.

The attacks 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' and 'file 08 edited' both fail: each clause 2 ends 'Condition 5 remains the only implementation authorization', each clause 3 is 'Does not edit file 08 (MF-6)', the header repeats '**Does not** edit file 08', and git reports zero modified tracked files across docs/v2/architecture, COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, the freeze and the blueprint.

The form claim is accurate against the right precedents. The header cites D-038 / D-039 / D-040 / D-041, of which D-039 and D-041 are the Route B disposition recordings — the same class of act. Adopted D-039's shape is: record the v2 disposition as the accepted draft its selection authorized; the row stays HARD-BLOCKED with condition 1 not discharging until owners record; does not edit file 08 (MF-6); Readiness effect Zero; Reversibility total with the overturn commit. D-049 and D-050 reproduce that shape clause for clause. D-039 carried an extra clause for an adopted rider because its review produced one; both v2s here were ACCEPT 0/0 with nothing owed, so there is correctly no rider and no advisory carry-list.

The Alternatives explain the absence of a carry-list rather than leaving it unstated: 'Record v1 with advisories owed. Rejected: v2 repaired both advisories and both reviewers ACCEPTed the repair.' That is accurate for my half on both rows — my v1 advisories C2-RB002-A1 and C2-RB004-A1 were repaired in v2 and I verified each repair at the bytes before returning ACCEPT.

Examined and dissolved by measurement, not asserted: D-039's clause 3 reads 'DR-005 stays HARD-BLOCKED / not SATISFIED' and its Alternatives reject marking SATISFIED, and neither appears in D-049 or D-050. I scanned all 38 adopted entries: exactly one carries a 'Mark … SATISFIED' rejection in its Alternatives, and exactly three say 'not SATISFIED' anywhere in the body. Neither is a convention of this class, so their absence here is not a departure from form. I set out to raise this and the measurement cut against it.

Reversibility is 'Total. Overturn: C-D049.' and 'Total. Overturn: C-D050.', matching adopted D-039 and D-041, which both read 'total. Overturn: C-D0xx.' for the same class. The compound form I required of D-046 and of D-048 does not apply here: those were acts whose overturn depends on a landed dependent, whereas recording an accepted draft that is expressly not owner recording leaves nothing dependent to unwind.
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex review of this subject. Not read; the file is confirmed absent at review time.

The Codex v2 reviews of either disposition, hashed but never opened. Both entries characterize them as ACCEPT 0/0. I verified the digests and not the verdict class or counts; if either characterization is wrong, the premise that no advisory remains owed fails, and nothing in my review would detect it.

Whether the Evidence authority, the V1 coordinator, or the Evidence/retention authority will record either disposition. Owner recording is the act these entries expressly are not, and my CONSENT is expressly not it either.

The merits of the two v2 dispositions beyond my separate reviews at 4619a113 and a2ab3306, whose stated limits I carry forward: I did not audit DR-124's current register standing beyond the disposition's own claim that it remains OPEN, and I did not assess whether either preview surface is under-inclusive.

Whether the four section31 v4 advisories the DR-004 disposition names as owed on Route A have moved since D-045. They are owed on that instrument's successor rather than on this recording, and neither entry claims otherwise.

consentNote: I CONSENT to both entries with zero findings, and I state what I attacked because a clean turn-1 consent on a paired recording deserves it. The axis most likely to fail here is the verdict class, and it is the one I can settle absolutely: my two v2 reviews were ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 advisories, and both entries say ACCEPT 0/0. Severability is structural rather than asserted, ACCEPT-as-owner-recording is foreclosed twice per entry plus once in each Alternatives list, and the owner strings agree across three documents. I did find two places where these entries are terser than D-039 — no 'not SATISFIED' beside HARD-BLOCKED and no rejected 'Mark SATISFIED' alternative — and rather than grade them from memory I counted across all 38 adopted entries, where those appear 3 times and once respectively. They are not conventions, so their absence is not a defect.
